Welcome to this journey where grief and identity are woven together in the most unexpected places—like the bustling aisles of a Korean grocery store. Imagine stepping into a world where every ingredient, every scent, and every shared meal carries the echo of memory and longing. That’s the heart of Michelle Zauner’s remarkable story, Crying in H Mart, where food isn’t just sustenance—it’s a portal to family, heritage, and the ache of losing someone you love.
Together, we’ll explore how the comfort of tradition gently meets the sharpness of loss, and how every ritual—every recipe—becomes a bridge to the past and a lifeline for the future. As we move through the flavors and textures of Korean cuisine, you’ll find they’re so much more than just dishes on a table. They’re the warmth of home, the bittersweet tug of change, and the way we keep our loved ones close, even when they’re gone.
Along the way, we’ll navigate what it means to grow up between cultures—the push and pull between fitting in and staying true to yourself. We’ll see how love can be shown in the smallest acts of care, sometimes unspoken, but always deeply felt. The story isn’t just about mourning; it’s about resilience, connection, and discovering who we are through what we remember, what we share, and what we carry forward.
So, let’s step into this world together. Let’s open ourselves to the beauty and pain of holding on, letting go, and finding our place within the enduring bonds of food, memory, and love.
